Subject: Dedicated pool onboarding — provisioning playbook & staged autoscale ramp

Hi Lara —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our handshake, I’m starting this thread to share the draft provisioning playbook and to lock in the staged autoscale/burst approach we discussed for your initial pilot region (us-west-2). High-level asks below so we can get ops and network engaged this week: 

- Target go-live window: week of Jan 25 (pilot load window Jan 25–29)
- Initial GPU pool shape: 8x A100s (single AZ), reserve 2 for warm standby
- Ramp plan: 2-week gradual traffic ramp with fixed quota growth (25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100%)
- Autoscale policy: scale-to-demand with hard burst cap at +50% capacity for 1 hour; fallback to smaller quantized model if capacity sustained >30m
- Network: please confirm peering window and NAT egress IP whitelist requirement

I’ve attached a short mutual action plan and a network topology stub for your infra team. Can you confirm: 1) the peering SLA (target date), 2) any procurement approval we should route (PO number), and 3) whether you want us to pre-warm KV cache for the first two days?

Once you confirm, I’ll loop in Monica (CS implementation lead) and the ops runbook owner to schedule the prep sprint.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Vanessa/Lara — short technical notes so Monica can fold these into the runbook: 

- Pool topology: recommend 6x A100 primary + 2x A100 warm standby (same AZ). Standby will hold warmed KV shards and be auto-attached on failover.
- Burst semantics: 50% additional capacity allowed for a single 60-minute window (as Vanessa wrote). If burst extends beyond 60m, autoscaler triggers cross-region spin-up to our compatible variant in us-east-1 (smaller quantized model with 10% quality delta).
- Autoscale metrics: use GPU utilization >60% sustained for 90s + queue depth >50 requests as scale-up signal. Cooldown: 3m for scale-down steps.
- Model fallback mapping: production model -> quantized-v2-0 (falls back automatically when scaled hosts < 70% of needed tokens/sec).

Monica — I put model/fallback IDs in the internal doc link here: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/acromed/fallbacks (please reference).

Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
